HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Night, medium close at the open timber gate of the fortress, torches on either side. Bidam with the slicked-back GREY hair and clean-shaven face of his sheet portrait, no headband, in his hybrid coat (white outer robe with galloping horses on the sleeves, deep navy lapel bands and navy shoulder yoke, plum inner robe), prayer beads on his wrist, no sword, lifts with both hands the face of the dead Yumjong (grey hair, his white robe with the crimson collar exactly as on his sheet portrait), who lies folded over a horse's saddle, eyes closed, black headband. Bidam's face: disbelief turning to grief, the smile gone. The horse's neck and mane fill the left foreground out of focus. Torch from the right as the hard key; navy #141C2E specular on the beads. ONE device: his two hands framing the dead face. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = bidam, SECOND face = yumjong. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_radiance_fortress (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels). BIDAM — Look: Tall, handsome, clean-shaven; short slicked-back black hair; warm brown eyes, faint self-amused smile. Dress: His signature hybrid coat: a long white outer robe whose wide sleeves are embroidered with galloping black horses, with deep navy #141C2E bands down the lapels and a navy yoke across the shoulders, over a plum-magenta inner robe and dark sash; the bead string looped on the right wrist. Navy lives only in those lapel and shoulder bands and on the beads — never a glow. Now: Older Sangdaedeung (stage portrait): grey at the temples, same smile. Colour #141C2E. YUMJONG Colour #8a68c9. PLACE Radiance Fortress (명활성) — attached board /pl_radiance_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Myeonghwal (Radiance) Fortress: Bidam's mountain wall facing Wolseong across the field. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
